question: How does oxygen concentration affect burn time in microgravity?
answer: In microgravity, enriched oxygen (33–40%) is associated with substantially longer burn times than air-like oxygen (18–23%). Across 179 ISS tests, the median burn time was 50.0 s at enriched oxygen versus 8.0 s at air-like oxygen, with maximums of 304.0 s versus 20.0 s. Every flame at air-like oxygen that ignited self-extinguished, whereas 30 enriched-oxygen tests were still burning when the fuel flow was cut. No tests exist between 23.5% and 33% oxygen, so the exact transition cannot be determined from these data. The 33–40% oxygen levels are ISS test-chamber conditions, not spacecraft cabin air (~21%).
